findings.situation: A filer paid their own parent $3,000 in cash in 2025 to care for the filer's child, and the conditions that make a parent's wages taxable do not apply, so no other test is met.
findings.source_text: f1040s2 Schedule 2 (2025), page 1, line 9: "Household employment taxes. Attach Schedule H"
findings.why: The help excludes only a spouse and a child under 21, so this filer answers Yes. Under the Schedule H rules that line 9 relies on, a parent's wages are generally excluded from the $2,800 test and from the $1,000 quarterly test, so no household employment tax is due. The question's own label also asks whether the filer 'owe[s] household employment taxes', which conflicts with the help.

findings.situation: A filer paid a 17-year-old who is not a student $3,000 for occasional yard work, and that work is not the young person's main occupation.
findings.source_text: f1040s2 Schedule 2 (2025), page 1, line 9: "Household employment taxes. Attach Schedule H"
findings.why: Under the Schedule H rule, wages to anyone under 18 are left out of the $2,800 test unless household work is that person's principal occupation. Being a student is only one sign that it is not. The help says 'leave out a student under 18', so this filer counts the pay and answers Yes when the line needs No.

locators: Schedule 2 (2025), line 9, "Household employment taxes. Attach Schedule H"
